name: Spearmint Energy (Spearmint Renewable Development Company, LLC and affiliates)
headquarters: Miami, Florida (2916 N. Miami Avenue); second office in Eden Prairie, Minnesota (7480 Flying Cloud Drive), per the company site
employees: Company boilerplate: 'over 70 professionals' (January 2026), 'over 60 professionals' (May–June 2026), 'over 50 professionals' (July 2026); PFI's 2024 profile put headcount at 34. No series is published and the 2026 figures move in the wrong direction for a growing company — treat as loosely stated.
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Spearmint Energy is a founder-led, trading-bred merchant developer that owns 350 MW / 700 MWh of two-hour ERCOT batteries (Revolution, Tierra Seca, Seven Flags), is building a fourth (Red Egret, 300 MW / 600 MWh, COD 2027), holds Minnesota's first two standalone-storage site permits (300 MW / 1,200 MWh), and has financed all of it without a single named offtaker, hedge or revenue put — on a USD 325 million private-credit platform facility, tax equity, a credit transfer and one undisclosed equity sale to Kyuden International. The premise '15 GWh in development' is the company's own boilerplate, stated in January and May 2026 and dropped from 21 May 2026 onward; the premise of a Blackstone sponsor is unsupported — no source links Blackstone to Spearmint, and the only ownership statement in the record is lender Elda River's that the company 'is controlled by Roscommon Analytics', an FTR and congestion trading firm founded by board chairman Kevin Kelley.

BACKGROUND. Launched in Miami in May 2022 by Andrew Waranch (Elustria, Elliott Associates, Deutsche Bank, Merrill Lynch, Constellation) with three stated strategies — development, storage offtake and power trading — Spearmint bought Revolution from Con Edison Development (July 2022), the 900 MW 'Nomadic' ERCOT portfolio (March 2023) and two Indiana projects from BW Solar (December 2023), then built Revolution to COD in January 2024 on Sungrow PowerTitan with Mortenson, financed by USD 92 million of Greenprint tax equity and a USD 200 million Aiga term loan later joined by Nuveen and Elda River. Tierra Seca and Seven Flags (USD 252 million from Manulife, East West Bank, Investec and Sugar Creek) reached COD in late December 2025, in the year Modo Energy puts ERCOT battery revenue at about USD 26–29 per kW against USD 193 per kW in 2023. Red Egret closed about USD 450 million on 21 May 2026 (a construction loan repaid at COD by Nuveen preferred equity and about USD 126 million of ITC transfer). Outside ERCOT: Snowshoe (permit August 2025) and Midwater (permit July 2026) in Minnesota, Pumpkinvine denied in Kokomo (November 2024), Silverfield in Kansas and Cloverleaf in South Dakota in development. Twenty executives and directors are named with photographs on the company's site; no CFO is listed.

Collection gaps: any revenue, dispatch result or contract price; the identity of the 'Nomadic' seller and the current status of the Cooke and Brazoria projects; the Kyuden stake and price; the Red Egret credit buyer; FERC market-based-rate or ERCOT QSE records (FERC pages unreadable); the CFO's successor; and the composition of the '15 GWh' beyond the projects named above.
ecosystemRole: Spearmint is the pure merchant case in this corpus's BESS buyer side: a developer that finances batteries on tax credits and private credit rather than utility contracts, procures from one integrator (Sungrow) and one EPC (Mortenson), and monetises through its own trading desk. For a supplier it is a repeat single-source account; for the market it is a small ERCOT owner whose fleet reached scale in the revenue trough; for the register it is the develop-to-hold merchant model that Aypa's contracted platform and Intersect's captive parks bracket.

productsAndServices.name: Owned and operated ERCOT battery fleet (merchant)
productsAndServices.description: Three operating standalone batteries in ERCOT, all two-hour, all built by Mortenson on Sungrow PowerTitan equipment, and all dispatched by Spearmint's own optimisation team without any named offtaker, hedge provider or revenue put: Revolution (150 MW / 300 MWh, McCamey, Upton County, in LCRA transmission territory next to the King Mountain wind farm; acquired as a development project from Con Edison Development in July 2022; commercial operation announced 4 January 2024 with 134 containers, 6,432 Sungrow modules and 45 PCS units), and Tierra Seca (Del Rio, Val Verde County) and Seven Flags (Laredo), 100 MW / 200 MWh each on PowerTitan 2.0, operating since late December 2025 per the company's 12 May 2026 release. Company boilerplate since May 2026: 'operates 350 MW / 700 MWh in ERCOT'.
highlights: The company's site says why merchant: it develops 'in locations where we can solve the biggest weaknesses of energy — intermittency and the price volatility it creates', while 'utilities, load-serving entities, and developers … given their lower risk tolerance, they are not as focused on deploying critical infrastructure in the regions with the greatest imbalances'.

No source names a tolling counterparty, hedge, revenue put or offtake for any ERCOT asset; the only tolling language in the record is the Minnesota Snowshoe application, which 'anticipates entering into a Tolling Agreement with its affiliated merchant energy business or similar third-party market participant'.

The two newest assets reached COD in ERCOT's 2025 revenue trough: Modo Energy puts 2025 ERCOT battery revenue at about USD 26–29 per kW against USD 193 per kW in 2023, and Enverus puts ancillary-service revenue down about 90 per cent since 2023.
Kyuden International (Kyushu Electric group) bought an undisclosed equity interest in Tierra Seca and Seven Flags in January 2026 — the only asset-level sale in the record.
productsAndServices.positioning: The smallest of the three merchant ERCOT storage owners in this corpus's IPP set by operating capacity (350 MW against Jupiter Power's fleet and Plus Power's contracted franchise), and the only one whose founder and board come from power trading rather than development — Roscommon Analytics, which lender Elda River says controls the company, is an FTR and congestion trading firm. Modo's ERCOT owner rankings do not list Spearmint.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: ERCOT day-ahead and real-time energy and ancillary-service markets via in-house dispatch ('Spearmint's internal software and associated forecasting tools', per the company's trader job posting); tax credits monetised through tax equity and transfer.
targetSegments: ERCOT wholesale market (energy arbitrage and ancillary services)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Red Egret (300 MW / 600 MWh, Texas City) under construction since May 2026 for a 2027 COD, taking the operating fleet to 'over 1.5 GWh … across four projects'.

productsAndServices.name: Development pipeline — MISO, SPP and beyond
productsAndServices.description: A pipeline the company has described as 2.8 GW (February 2024), 4.1 GW (July 2024), 'over 13 GWh' in ten states (April and September 2025) and 'over 15 GWh' across more than 20 projects in 12–13 states (January and May 2026), then without a gigawatt-hour figure from 21 May 2026 onward ('projects under development throughout the United States'). Named projects outside ERCOT per regulator and county records: Snowshoe (150 MW / 600 MWh, Olmsted County, Minnesota — MPUC docket IP-7138/ESS-24-279, site permit August 2025, the state's first standalone battery permit, estimated capital cost USD 214 million in the application, COD Q4 2027, MISO queue J2731 via SMMPA's Maple Leaf substation); Midwater (150 MW / 600 MWh, Freeborn County, Minnesota — MPUC dockets 24-294/24-295, site permit 16 July 2026 with insurance, decommissioning and fire-coordination conditions, about USD 457 million capital cost per press reading of the filings, COD end-2027); Pumpkinvine (up to 400 MW, Howard County, Indiana — MISO queue J2766; Kokomo rezoning denied unanimously 12 November 2024); Green Eagle (125 MW, Indiana, bought with Pumpkinvine from BW Solar in December 2023); Silverfield (300 MW / 1,200 MWh, Linn County, Kansas, presented March 2025, target 2028); Cloverleaf (up to 175 MW, Brookings County, South Dakota, at the MISO–SPP seam). The 900 MW / 2,000 MWh 'Nomadic' ERCOT portfolio bought in March 2023 (Cooke, Galveston, Brazoria Counties) has no later status under that name.
highlights: The company has never itemised the 15 GWh: the identifiable pieces are 350 MW / 700 MWh operating, 300 MW / 600 MWh under construction, 300 MW / 1,200 MWh permitted in Minnesota and the Indiana, Kansas and South Dakota projects above.
Both Minnesota applications were designed around Tesla Megapack 2XL enclosures 'to allow flexibility during equipment selection' — a design basis, not an order.
Waranch's stated geography (2024): ERCOT first, SPP and MISO 'significant potential', NYISO for acquisitions, 'we opt out of' PJM, California limited.

Buy-side M&A is the sourcing method: Revolution from Con Edison Development (2022), Nomadic from an unnamed 'major developer' (2023), Green Eagle and Pumpkinvine from BW Solar (2023); Energy-Storage.news notes an earlier Black Mountain Energy Storage / Cypress Creek exclusivity on the Tierra Seca and Seven Flags sites that Spearmint did not explain.
productsAndServices.positioning: A develop-to-own pipeline assembled largely by buying other developers' early-stage projects, financed on a platform term loan rather than sponsor equity; the Minnesota permits are the first standalone-storage site permits in that state.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Held in project LLCs under Spearmint Renewable Development Company, LLC (Snowshoe BESS, LLC; Midwater BESS, LLC; Tierra Seca BESS LLC).
targetSegments: County and state permitting authorities (Minnesota PUC, Texas cities, Indiana and Kansas counties)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Snowshoe and Midwater construction Q1 2027, COD late 2027; Silverfield 2028; Cloverleaf's SPP phase was stated for Q1 2026 and MISO phase Q1 2028 in 2024 press, with no permit outcome found.

productsAndServices.name: Optimisation and trading (the 'affiliated merchant energy business')
productsAndServices.description: Spearmint launched in May 2022 describing three strategies — 'battery and solar project development, energy storage offtake, and renewables power trading' — and Waranch's 2022 op-ed proposed 'providing tolling solutions for developers via renting the battery facility' so that builders 'achieve lower borrowing costs'. By 2026 the arm is described as Optimization: Nick Dazzo (Managing Director, Head of Optimization) 'focuses on contracting for battery offtake and associated risk management activity'; Jason Gran (Head of Research, ex-Wärtsilä) runs 'forecasting and optimization technology'; the August 2026 'Power Energy Storage Trader' posting describes 'dispatching Spearmint's battery storage assets … execute energy and ancillary service offers in day-ahead and real-time markets, utilizing Spearmint's internal software and associated forecasting tools … around-the-clock physical dispatch', with 'familiarity with futures and other hedging markets' preferred.
highlights: The board is a trading board: chairman Kevin Kelley founded Roscommon Analytics ('power optimization including FTRs and congestion'); John Rittenhouse founded and ran EDF Trading for 21 years; Waranch's own career ran through Elustria, Elliott Associates, Deutsche Bank, Merrill Lynch and Constellation Energy.

No third-party offtake customer of the trading arm, no FERC market-based-rate authorisation and no ERCOT QSE registration for a Spearmint entity was found (FERC pages returned 403 — unverified, not absent; ERCOT assets do not need FERC MBR).

PFI's 2024 profile called Spearmint a 'green merchant energy trading company' and referred to 'an innovative, creditworthy offtake structure' and 'a merchant trading component with hedging' without naming counterparties.
productsAndServices.positioning: The optimisation arm is what lets a founder-led company finance merchant batteries: lenders underwrite the dispatch team and the platform, not a PPA. Whether it tolls third-party batteries, as the 2022 thesis proposed, is not evidenced.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal dispatch of owned assets; the Snowshoe application anticipates a tolling agreement between the project company and the 'affiliated merchant energy business'.
targetSegments: Third-party developers (proposed in 2022; no customer found)
productsAndServices.roadmap: None stated beyond hiring; the company added 'provide system stability for new large loads' to its boilerplate in 2026 and Waranch reports 'more and more RFPs from tech companies'.

productsAndServices.name: Capital structure — platform debt, project debt, tax equity and credit transfer
productsAndServices.description: Every dollar in the record is a debt, tax-equity or project-equity instrument; no corporate equity round, valuation or sponsor commitment has ever been announced. Platform level: a USD 200 million term loan from Aiga Capital Partners (June 2023), joined by Nuveen Energy Infrastructure Credit as co-anchor (February 2024) and Elda River Capital Management (July 2024), then a USD 325 million 'expanded debt facility' with Nuveen, Elda River, Harrison Street Asset Management and Aiga (23 June 2026). Project level: USD 92 million of tax equity from Greenprint Capital Management for Revolution (October 2023) and USD 48 million from Manulife (per the company's news archive); USD 252 million for Tierra Seca and Seven Flags (April 2025 — USD 59 million construction-to-term loans from Manulife, USD 95 million tax-equity bridge loans from East West Bank and Investec, USD 98 million of tax-equity commitments from Sugar Creek Capital); a Kyuden International equity investment in the same two projects (January 2026, terms undisclosed); and about USD 450 million for Red Egret (21 May 2026 — a USD 225 million construction facility led by First Citizens and Investec with Nord/LB and East West Bank, to be repaid at COD by USD 96 million of Nuveen preferred equity and about USD 126 million of ITC-transfer proceeds from an unnamed buyer).
highlights: Greenprint's Revolution investment was described by Energy-Storage.news as 'one of the first applications' of the standalone-storage ITC after the IRA.

Red Egret's structure — construction loan taken out at COD by preferred equity plus a credit transfer, with no term debt named — is the record's clearest example of financing a merchant battery without a PPA.

Lender Elda River's case study states the company 'is controlled by Roscommon Analytics, a large commodity trading platform' — the only ownership statement in any source; the company itself names no owner. The brief's Blackstone premise is unsupported: no source links Blackstone to Spearmint.
Waranch (2024): merchant-only projects appeal to 'approximately 20%' of available investors; offtake 'reduce[s] merchant revenue risk, attracting broader investor base'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Where Aypa finances on utility contracts and a USD 1.5 billion warehouse, Spearmint finances on private credit (Aiga, Nuveen, Elda River, Harrison Street), regional and foreign banks (Manulife, East West Bank, Investec, First Citizens, Nord/LB), tax-equity boutiques (Greenprint, Sugar Creek) and a Japanese utility's equity — a merchant developer's stack.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bilateral platform facilities and project-level syndicates; counsel Paul Hastings on every deal.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The June 2026 facility is described as growth capital for the operating portfolio and 'US development portfolio'; no equity raise is announced.

relationships.scale: 'more than 1 GWh of additional energy storage capacity … through 2025' (2024 partnership); 149 PowerTitan 2.0 units at Red Egret; all four ERCOT projects
relationships.note: Sungrow supplied Revolution (PowerTitan: 6,432 modules, 134 containers, 45 PCS), Tierra Seca and Seven Flags (PowerTitan 2.0) and Red Egret (149 PowerTitan 2.0 units), under a Texas partnership for more than 1 GWh announced in August 2024.
relationships.context: The relationship is the fleet: every Spearmint battery in Texas is a Sungrow system, and Spearmint's May 2026 release calls Red Egret 'the fourth Spearmint project to use the PowerTitan platform supplied by Sungrow USA'. CleanTechnica's account of the September 2024 partnership quotes Peter Rood and Sungrow's Martial Yu on more than 1 GWh of additional Texas capacity through 2025. The Minnesota projects, by contrast, are designed around Tesla Megapack 2XL. Waranch's statement that the company began 'evaluating suppliers all over the world' in May 2024 for FEOC reasons is the one signal that the concentration may not persist.

relationships.note: Mortenson built Revolution (EPC signed November 2022, Mortenson's 20th battery project), Tierra Seca and Seven Flags, and is building Red Egret, 'the fourth project built for Spearmint by Minneapolis-based M.A. Mortenson Company'.
relationships.context: EnergyTech reported the Revolution EPC in December 2022; Spearmint's 12 May 2026 COD release quotes Mortenson's Kevin Boyce (VP and GM, Energy Storage) on Tierra Seca and Seven Flags; the Red Egret financing release names Mortenson as EPC again. Spearmint's second office is in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, near Mortenson's Minneapolis base. No other EPC appears in the record.

relationships.note: Spearmint's Minnesota PUC applications model the Snowshoe and Midwater layouts on Tesla Megapack 2XL enclosures while reserving equipment selection until construction — a design basis in a regulator's record, not a supply contract.
relationships.context: The Snowshoe application (October 2024) states the preliminary design is based on Tesla Megapack 2 XL 'to allow flexibility during equipment selection'; Energy-Storage.news reports the same basis for Midwater from the MPUC filings. Neither Tesla nor Spearmint has announced an order. It is nonetheless the only non-Sungrow equipment named for any Spearmint project, and the Minnesota permits are the company's only post-ERCOT capacity.

relationships.note: Modo Energy's 2025 ERCOT buildout report lists Jupiter Power among the ISO's major battery owners alongside Engie, Enel, SMT and Tesla, in a market where Spearmint's 350 MW does not appear in the rankings.
relationships.context: Spearmint and Jupiter Power run the same business — merchant batteries in ERCOT dispatched by an in-house trading team — at different scale. Modo's annual report puts ERCOT at 13.9 GW / 22.9 GWh entering 2026, with Engie at about 20 per cent share and new entrants including esVolta, Intersect, Gridstor, Nightpeak, TotalEnergies, Eni, Equinor, Brookfield and Tokyo Gas America; Spearmint's 350 MW is about 2.5 per cent of the fleet by arithmetic and is not named.

relationships.note: Modo Energy's 2025 ERCOT buildout report names Intersect among the year's new battery-owner entrants — three 160 MW / 320 MWh merchant batteries on Tesla Autobidder, the same merchant model Spearmint runs on Sungrow.
relationships.context: Both companies argued the merchant case in the founder's voice — Kimber's 'long-term offtake contracts actually destroy value' and Waranch's 'utilities … are not as focused on deploying critical infrastructure in the regions with the greatest imbalances' — and both financed ERCOT batteries on tax equity and private credit. Intersect's batteries moved to IPX Power in March 2026; the comparison is of models, not a commercial tie.

policyExposure.exposure: Revolution's USD 92 million Greenprint tax-equity investment (October 2023) was described by Energy-Storage.news as 'one of the first applications of the new standalone [storage] ITC'; Tierra Seca and Seven Flags carry USD 98 million of Sugar Creek tax-equity commitments bridged by East West Bank and Investec; Red Egret's USD 225 million construction loan is to be repaid at COD partly by about USD 126 million of ITC-transfer proceeds from an unnamed buyer. Waranch: 'we pioneer innovative approaches to monetise tax credits'.

policyExposure.regime: OBBBA (HR1) — credit phase-down and FEOC restrictions
policyExposure.exposure: All four ERCOT projects use Sungrow PowerTitan equipment, and the two Minnesota projects are designed around Tesla Megapack 2XL. Waranch, in Troutman Pepper Locke's September 2025 report: storage 'remained relatively unscathed'; FEOC is 'unquestionably a big issue'; 'our team took aggressive action in May 2024 … we started evaluating suppliers all over the world' (Europe, Japan, Korea); investors 'stopped sitting on their wallets' once 'the OBBBA gave people some clarity'. No source quantifies Spearmint's FEOC exposure or names a non-Chinese supplier it has contracted.
policyExposure.mitigation: Supplier diversification search begun May 2024 (company statement); no contract announced

policyExposure.regime: ERCOT market design — ancillary-service saturation and Real-Time Co-optimization plus Batteries (RTC+B)
policyExposure.exposure: Spearmint's entire operating fleet is merchant ERCOT storage. Modo Energy puts 2025 ERCOT battery revenue at about USD 26–29 per kW against USD 56 per kW in 2024 and USD 193 per kW in 2023, with ancillary-service revenue at USD 0.50 per kW-month in October 2025 against USD 1.52 a year earlier and the West load zone (Revolution's) the strongest at USD 3.4 per kW-month; Enverus puts ancillary-service revenue down about 90 per cent since 2023 with the ancillary share of revenue falling from 84 to 48 per cent, and RTC+B scheduled for December 2025. Modo's outlook cites load growth, thermal retirements, HB 1500 firming and 'volatility swaps, revenue-sharing arrangements' as bridges.

policyExposure.regime: Texas SB 6 and HB 1500 (large loads, firming, curtailment)
policyExposure.exposure: Spearmint's 2026 boilerplate adds 'provide system stability for new large loads' and Waranch reports 'more and more RFPs from tech companies'; HB 1500's firming obligation is one of the revenue drivers Modo names. No Spearmint project is a co-located load and no SB 6 filing names the company.

policyExposure.regime: Minnesota PUC site permitting (first standalone BESS permits in the state)
policyExposure.exposure: Snowshoe (docket IP-7138/ESS-24-279) received Minnesota's first standalone-battery site permit in August 2025 with emergency-response, water-main and first-responder-training conditions; Midwater (dockets 24-294/24-295) followed on 16 July 2026 with stormwater basins, insurance through decommissioning, a decommissioning and remediation fund and fire-department coordination, after residents 'made their voices heard' (Commissioner Tuma). Both applications state the projects will sell 'on a merchant basis' through a tolling agreement with the affiliated merchant business.

policyExposure.regime: Local zoning and fire-safety approvals (Indiana, Texas, Kansas, South Dakota)
policyExposure.exposure: Kokomo's plan commission denied Pumpkinvine's rezoning unanimously on 12 November 2024 after a petition of about 1,000 signatures and a hired attorney, citing fire risk and proximity to homes and a BorgWarner plant, with a six-month reapplication bar; Texas City approved Red Egret on 7 August 2025 only after 'a prior proposal was reworked after city feedback' and under a new 'District S-P' battery zoning; Linn County, Kansas noted 'ongoing community debate'; Cloverleaf had no permit application as of November 2024.

Waranch's Utility Dive op-ed asked whether the grid 'will be determined by free market competition or by monopoly utilities', criticised PJM's Reliability Resource Initiative as queue-jumping and called on FERC to 'reaffirm its commitment to market competition — and prevent utility self-dealing'. No FERC market-based-rate authorisation for a Spearmint entity was found (FERC pages returned 403; unverified rather than absent). Regulatory affairs is led by Jack Clark III, ex-NextEra.

periods.commentary: Spearmint publishes no accounts. The stack that can be read from releases — a USD 325 million platform facility, roughly USD 800 million of project-level debt, tax equity and credit transfer, and one undisclosed strategic equity sale — is a merchant developer's, and the two figures that would test it (ERCOT revenue per kW at Revolution, and the price Kyuden paid) are not public. 'Expected' is left empty throughout; no consensus or guidance exists.

financials.commentary: What is knowable: the company has financed four ERCOT batteries totalling 650 MW / 1,300 MWh without a named offtaker, using tax equity, bank construction loans, private-credit platform debt, preferred equity and a credit transfer. What is not: revenue, dispatch performance, the owner's identity in the company's own words, or who bought the Red Egret credits.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Spearmint is a develop-to-hold merchant owner, not a develop-to-sell developer. Basis: every boilerplate since 2024 reads 'developing, owning, operating, and optimizing'; the only sell-side transaction in the record is a partial post-COD equity sale to Kyuden; the pipeline was assembled by buying other developers' projects (Con Edison Development, the 'Nomadic' seller, BW Solar), not by selling its own. The brief's develop-to-sell framing should be read as the model Spearmint buys from, not the one it runs.

(High confidence) We assess that no sponsor stands behind the company in the way the brief supposed. Basis: no Blackstone reference exists in any source; the company names no owner; the single ownership statement is Elda River's 'controlled by Roscommon Analytics'; the board carries two Bain Capital-affiliated directors and an Encompass Capital partner without any stated shareholding. The capital is debt and tax equity, not sponsor equity.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the fleet's realised revenue in 2025–2026 is well below what it was underwritten on, and that the June 2026 facility expansion is partly a liquidity response. Basis: Modo's and Enverus's 2025 ERCOT figures (revenue down about 84 per cent from 2023; ancillary revenue down about 90 per cent), the timing of Tierra Seca and Seven Flags' COD in December 2025, and the USD 325 million facility described as 'growth capital' for the operating and development portfolios. No Spearmint revenue figure exists to confirm it.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the 'over 15 GWh' pipeline is a development-stage inventory, most of it early, and that its removal from the boilerplate on 21 May 2026 was deliberate. Basis: the identifiable pieces sum to 1.3 GWh operating or under construction, 1.2 GWh permitted, and Indiana, Kansas and South Dakota projects at pre-permit stage; the figure rose from 10 to 13 to 15 GWh in eighteen months as headcount fell from 'over 70' to 'over 50'; the company has never itemised it.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that supplier concentration in Sungrow is the fleet's largest policy exposure and that the May 2024 supplier search has not yet produced a contract. Basis: four of four ERCOT projects on PowerTitan; the Minnesota designs on Tesla Megapack 2XL as a basis only; Waranch's own statement that FEOC is 'unquestionably a big issue'; no non-Chinese order announced.

(Low confidence) We assess that the trading arm does not toll third-party batteries, despite the 2022 thesis. Basis: no third-party customer, FERC market-based-rate record or ERCOT QSE registration was found, and the only tolling language is between a project company and 'its affiliated merchant energy business'. The FERC record was unreadable, so this is an absence of evidence.

Indicators to watch: (1) Red Egret's COD against the 2027 company date and the 31 August 2026 interconnection-agreement date reported by Energy-Storage.news — a slip past 2027 would indicate construction-loan stress; (2) the name of the Red Egret ITC buyer or any FEOC-compliant supply contract, which would resolve the concentration judgment; (3) a named CFO, and any restatement of headcount above 'over 50'; (4) a first MISO financing for Snowshoe or Midwater (construction stated for Q1 2027) — a third-party tolling counterparty in that financing would refute the captive-tolling judgment; (5) Kyuden or another utility taking a further stake, or a whole-project sale, which would move the company toward develop-to-sell; (6) ERCOT revenue recovery signals Modo names — RTC+B, HB 1500 firming, load growth — against which the 2027 fleet of 1.3 GWh is levered.
